item.title: Digitally Optimized Initializations for Fast Thermodynamic Computing
item.description: arXiv:2603.24183v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thermodynamic computing harnesses the relaxation dynamics of physical systems to perform matrix operations. A key limitation of such approaches is the often long thermalization time required for the system to approach equilibrium with sufficient accuracy. Here, we introduce a hybrid digital-thermodynamic algorithm that substantially accelerates relaxation through optimized initializations inspired by the Mpemba effect. In the proposed scheme, a classical digital processor efficiently computes an initialization that suppresses slow relaxation modes, after which the physical system performs the remaining computation through its intrinsic relaxation dynamics. We focus on overdamped Langevin dynamics for quadratic energy landscapes, analyzing the spectral structure of the associated Fokker-Planck operator and identifying the corresponding optimal initial covariances. This yields a predictable reduction in thermalization time, determined by the spectrum of the encoded matrix. We derive analytic expressions for the resulting speedups and numerically analyze thermodynamic implementations of matrix inversion and determinant computation as concrete examples. Our results show that optimized initialization protocols provide a simple and broadly applicable route to accelerating thermodynamic computations.
item.dc:creator: Mattia Moroder, Felix C. Binder, John Goold

item.title: The Mpemba effect likes to hit a wall
item.description: arXiv:2604.01543v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The original Mpemba effect refers to the counterintuitive possibility that a system prepared at a higher temperature relaxes to a colder equilibrium faster than one prepared at a lower temperature. In microscopic classical realizations, this phenomenon has been studied for overdamped particles in external potentials and observed experimentally. We show that, for a particle in an asymmetric polynomial double-well potential, the one-dimensional Mpemba effect is controlled not by the double-well structure or metastability itself, but by the high-energy confinement: a hard boundary, or more generally a sufficiently steep confining tail, on the shallow side can induce the required population inversion. For the polynomial potentials considered here, the effect disappears when both hard boundaries are taken to infinity, whereas sufficiently asymmetric soft tails can play the same role as walls. We identify the underlying mechanism as a redistribution of the initial equilibrium population when it begins to probe the high-energy tails of the potential, a picture that also extends to single-well and symmetric double-well potentials.
item.dc:creator: Yue Liu, Tan Van Vu, Rapha\"el Ch\'etrite, Fr\'ed\'eric van Wijland, Hisao Hayakawa

item.title: Optimization of current-based sensing of phonon temperature using a finite reservoir
item.description: arXiv:2604.28155v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In realistic nanoscale transport set-ups, electron-phonon coupling leads to the exchange of heat between phonon baths and electronic reservoirs with finite heat capacities. Such exchange affects the finite reservoir's temperature. However, this sensitivity of the finite reservoir temperature to the exchange of heat with the finite reservoir has remained unexplored for thermometry. Here, we fill this gap by combining current metrology techniques with a thermodynamic framework encompassing finite reservoirs. We focus on an experimentally realizable set-up with a quantum dot coupled to a finite reservoir and consider two distinct current-based strategies in the long time limit, namely monitoring quanta exchanged between the quantum dot and finite reservoir and the measurement of the total current flowing from the quantum dot into an infinite reservoir. A third strategy involves measurements of the quantum dot occupation. For a large but finite reservoir, we show that the Fisher information for all three strategies captures the finite reservoir's contribution to sensitivity through common factors. We also demonstrate that monitoring quanta exchanged between the system and finite reservoir in the long time limit achieves optimal precision. Finally, we provide an optimization analysis that explores how maximal precision can be achieved within each of the current-based strategies by tuning the gate voltage.
item.dc:creator: Sindre Brattegard, Stephanie Matern, Mark T. Mitchison, Saulo V. Moreira

item.title: Predicting the conditions for observing the Mpemba effect
item.description: arXiv:2606.03445v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Mpemba effect, a counterintuitive phenomenon where a hotter system relaxes faster than a colder one, has been widely observed in various nonequilibrium systems. Despite this progress, the fundamental structural features of the energy landscape required for its emergence remain a subject of debate. In this study, we investigate the conditions for the Mpemba effect within one-dimensional overdamped Langevin dynamics. We classify the potential landscapes based on the presence of single or double wells, their symmetry properties, and the existence of walls. We establish that the existence of the effect is primarily driven by the presence of boundaries, either hard or soft, rather than the specific internal structure of the potential landscape, such as metastability or the number of minima. By employing a spectral decomposition of the Fokker-Planck operator, we analyze the behavior of the first nontrivial eigenmode and demonstrate that its derivative acts as a Dirac delta peak in the low-temperature regime. This helps us elucidate the mechanism underlying the Mpemba effect: it appears as the interplay between this behavior and the initial population dynamics in a non-trivial way induced by the presence of the wall. Our analysis provides a unified classification across single- and double-well potentials, highlighting the crucial role of boundary conditions and asymmetry. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this framework allows for the engineering of potential landscapes capable of producing multistage Mpemba transitions.
item.dc:creator: Yue Liu, Tan Van Vu, Rapha\"el Ch\'etrite, Fr\'ed\'eric van Wijland, Hisao Hayakawa

item.title: Nonlocal fractional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang dynamics of grain boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2606.21903v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The kinetic roughening of driven grain boundaries (GBs) is mediated by the collective behavior of disconnections, whose long-range 1/r elastic interactions distinguish them from conventional growing surfaces. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations show that the roughness of driven GBs undergoes a sharp crossover as the applied strain increases, with the Hurst exponent (H) increasing from approximately 0.33 to 0.8. We develop a nonlocal fractional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (fKPZ) theory to describe this low-temperature behavior, where the 1/r nonlocal elasticity behaves as the fractional relaxation of the GB morphology. The results show that the spatially-correlated noise associated with disconnection avalanches interacts with the KPZ nonlinearity to produce the post-crossover roughening observed in atomistic simulations. The post-crossover roughness exponent (H ~ 0.8) is comparable to values reported for dynamic fracture, suggesting the underlying physics shared by the collective behavior of defects (e.g., disconnections, dislocations) and interfacial roughening.
item.dc:creator: Kai Zhao

item.title: Statistical properties of quadrangular surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.19221v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the statistical properties of random quadrangular surfaces generated by different randomization procedures: the Gruzberg-Kl\"umper-Nuding-Sedrakyan (GKNS) construction, and two newly introduced generalizations of dynamical triangulations (DT), dynamical (DQ) and general quadrangulations (GQ). We formulate these surfaces within a unified graph-theoretic framework and establish the relationships between the elementary operations defining the different ensembles. For GKNS surfaces, we demonstrate that the construction is equivalent to two mutually constrained percolation processes and determine the associated critical point and critical exponents, revealing deviations from ordinary percolation. For DQ and GQ, we analyze the underlying Markov chains and determine the scaling of mixing and relaxation times. We further analyze all three ensembles through their degree distributions, degree correlations, distance statistics, and Hausdorff dimensions. While DQ exhibits exponentially decaying degree distributions and geometric properties similar to DT, GKNS and GQ display broad, scale-free degree distributions. Moreover, GKNS surfaces possess an asymptotic Hausdorff dimension $\Delta_H\approx 2$, whereas DQ and GQ approach $\Delta_H\approx 4$, similarly to DT. This indicates that DQ is compatible with the universal behavior of DT, while GKNS and GQ define distinct classes of random geometry, implying a different underlying measure in the space of random surfaces and a possible geometric framework for a new class of noncritical string theories.
item.dc:creator: Hrant Topchyan, Rudik Badalyan, Ara Sedrakyan

item.title: Non-Hermitian Random Matrix Theory of Jamming in Active Disordered Media
item.description: arXiv:2607.26406v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a non-Hermitian random-matrix description of active jammed systems in which a passive Wishart operator is perturbed by non-reciprocal Ginibre couplings. Within a Hermitized self-consistent Born approximation (SCBA), we derive a scalar susceptibility equation predicting \(J\sim\alpha_0^{-6/7}\) at the marginal point. Direct random-matrix calculations confirm that the mechanically relevant response is governed by singular values rather than complex eigenvalues. They further reveal strong finite-size fluctuations: near marginality, a large fraction of the total susceptibility is typically carried by the smallest singular value. These results distinguish the smooth large-\(N_c\) SCBA response from the extreme singular-value statistics of finite non-Hermitian systems.
item.dc:creator: Hisao Hayakawa

item.title: Exact expressions of correlation functions between two spins in the boundary row of the two-dimensional rectangular Ising model with periodic-free boundary conditions and finite size
item.description: arXiv:2608.19274v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present exact expressions of correlation functions between two spins in the boundary row of the two-dimensional rectangular Ising model with periodic-free boundary conditions and finite size. Some properties of exact expressions obtained are discussed. The fundamental property of the Ising model that the long range order emerge as the temperature decrease is shown clearly; expressions of the correlation functions in the thermodynamic limit varies depending on the order of taking limits of two parameters L and N; the impact of different sizes on correlation functions is illustrated with the aid of diagrams. Expressions of the correlation function discussed in this paper in the thermodynamic limit has been presented by previous researchers, and we prove that expressions obtained in this article is identical in form to expressions provided by previous researchers in the thermodynamic limit.
item.dc:creator: Mei Tao

item.title: de Almeida-Thouless Stability and Replica Symmetry Breaking in a Hybrid Watermarking Model with Image and Message Decoding
item.description: arXiv:2609.06405v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the de Almeida-Thouless (AT) stability of the replica symmetric (RS) solution for a spread-spectrum watermarking model incorporating Bayes-estimation-based image restoration. In our previously proposed model [1], which simultaneously performs message decoding and image restoration under Gaussian channel noise, a discrepancy between the theoretical predictions of the RS solution and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations was observed in specific parameter regimes. In this paper, by analyzing the blind case where both the original message and image are unknown, we explicitly derive the conditions for the AT stability of the RS solution by clarifying the structure of the replicon eigenspace for the hybrid system. Our results reveal that AT stability is broken precisely in the parameter region where the RS solution deviates from MCMC simulations, thereby successfully explaining the mechanism underlying this discrepancy in terms of replica symmetry breaking (RSB). [1] M. Kawamura, T. Uezu, K. Hayashi, and M. Okada, ``Statistical mechanical evaluation of a spread-spectrum watermarking model with image restoration,'' Phys. Rev. E \textbf{99}, 062132 (2019).
item.dc:creator: Tatsuya Uezu, Kao Hayashi, Masaki Kawamura

item.title: Trajectory Statistics Govern Mechanical Power Transfer in Active Baths
item.description: arXiv:2609.17047v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In active media, a moving passive object can experience negative drag and receive positive mechanical power from the bath, in contrast to the dissipative response in equilibrium. For a probe moving at velocity $\mathbf{V}$ and interacting weakly with an ideal active bath, we show that free-particle trajectory statistics determine the density response and the resulting bath force. The probe--particle interaction sets the wave-vector weighting, while the imposed motion selects frequencies $\omega_{\mathbf q}=\mathbf q\cdot \mathbf V$, separating bath dynamics from probe properties. The sign of the response spectrum yields probe-independent constraints for mechanical power transfer. Applying this framework to representative active-particle models reveals distinct power-transfer behavior despite identical displacement variances. For prescribed probe motion, the relation predicts drag reversal, motion-induced density distortions, and velocity-dependent friction, in quantitative agreement with simulations. Beyond the mean force, the free-particle trajectory statistics also determine the force autocorrelation. These results provide a route to predict the mechanical response of probes from single-particle trajectory statistics measured in the absence of the probe.
item.dc:creator: Chul-Ung Woo, Jiwon Choi, Heiko Rieger

item.title: Thermal conductivity of Lennard-Jones fluids from equilibrium thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.41952v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a general expression for the thermal conductivity of simple fluids within a thermodynamic transport theory (TTT) in which the Onsager coefficients of an interacting system are related to those of an ideal reference system through the ratio of the determinants of the Hessians of the relevant thermodynamic potential. The transported quantity is identified with an effective energy density proportional to the rms energy fluctuations of a small fluid cell. The result expresses the thermal conductivity as the product of its dilute-gas value and a function of equilibrium thermodynamic properties, namely the specific heats at constant density and at constant $\rho T$ and the temperature derivative of the latter, with no adjustable parameters. For hard spheres, it reduces to a previously verified expression in terms of the thermodynamic factor. The theory is tested against molecular dynamics results for the Lennard-Jones (LJ) and the truncated and shifted Lennard-Jones (LJTS) fluids in the supercritical region, for densities up to $\rho^*=0.8$, using equations of state based on perturbation theory. For the LJTS fluid, the mean absolute percentage error is below 8\% for all the temperatures considered. For the LJ fluid, the predictions are compared with those of the revised Enskog theory for Mie fluids, using the same equation of state: TTT gives smaller errors at almost all temperatures, with a significant improvement at low temperatures, where the errors are reduced approximately by a factor between two and three.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Hoyuelos, Alejandro Al\'es

item.title: Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.03857v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Brollo

item.title: Macroscopic diffusive fluctuations for generalized hard rods dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2305.13037v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the fluctuations in equilibrium for a dynamics of rods with random length. This includes the classical hard rod elastic collisions, when rod lengths are constant and equal to a positive value. We prove that in the diffusive space-time scaling, an initial fluctuation of density of particles of velocity $v$, after recentering on its Euler evolution, evolve randomly shifted by a Brownian motion of variance $\mathcal D(v)$.
item.dc:creator: Pablo A. Ferrari, Stefano Olla

item.title: Symmetries, correlation functions, and entanglement of general quantum Motzkin spin-chains
item.description: arXiv:2408.16070v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motzkin spin-chains, which include `colorless' (integer spin $s=1$) and `colorful' ($s \geq 2$) variants, are one-dimensional (1D) local integer spin models notable for their lack of a conformal field theory (CFT) description of their low-energy physics, despite being gapless. The colorful variants are particularly unusual, as they exhibit power-law violation of the area-law of entanglement entropy (as $\sqrt{n}$ in system size $n$), rather than a logarithmic violation as seen in a CFT. In this work, we analytically discover several unique properties of these models, potentially suggesting a new universality class for their low-energy physics. We identify a complex structure of symmetries and unexpected scaling behavior in spin-spin correlations, which deviate from known 1D universality classes. Specifically, the $s=1$ chain exhibits $U(1)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking and ferromagnetic order. Meanwhile, the $s \geq 2$ chains do not appear to spontaneously break any symmetries, but display quasi-long-range algebraic order with power-law decaying correlations, inconsistent with standard Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) critical exponents. We also derive asymptotic scaling expressions, with explicit additive constants, for entanglement measures in both colorless and colorful chains, generalizing previous results of Movassagh [J. Math Phys. (2017)], while providing benchmarks for potential quantum simulation experiments. The $\sqrt{n}$ entanglement scaling implies that any matrix-product-state description of these ground states requires bond dimension $e^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$; this superpolynomial cost of the standard 1D tensor-network toolkit, along with the analytical tractability of their ground state properties, positions Motzkin spin chains as intriguing testbeds for quantum simulation of many-body physics.
item.dc:creator: Varun Menon, Andi Gu, Ramis Movassagh

item.title: Optimal Calibration of Qubit Detuning and Crosstalk
item.description: arXiv:2507.10661v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Characterizing and calibrating physical qubits is essential for maintaining the performance of quantum processors. A key challenge in this process is the presence of crosstalk that complicates the estimation of individual qubit detunings. In this work, we derive optimal strategies for estimating detuning and crosstalk parameters by optimizing Ramsey interference experiments using Fisher information and the Cramer-Rao bound. We compare several calibration protocols, including measurements of a single quadrature at multiple times and of two quadratures at a single time, for a fixed number of total measurements. Our results predict that the latter approach yields the highest precision and robustness in both cases of isolated and coupled qubits. We validate experimentally our approach using a single NV center as well as superconducting transmons. Our approach enables accurate parameter extraction with significantly fewer measurements, resulting in up to a 50% reduction in calibration time while maintaining estimation accuracy.
item.dc:creator: David Shnaiderov, Matan Ben Dov, Yoav Woldiger, Assaf Hamo, Eugene Demler, Emanuele G. Dalla Torre

item.title: Learning to stabilize nonequilibrium phases of matter with active feedback using partial information
item.description: arXiv:2508.06612v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advances in quantum computing experiments have enabled new pathways for feedback control. Here, we investigate the role of information in interactive quantum many-body dynamics to engineer out-of-equilibrium phases of matter. To this end, we train reinforcement learning agents to prevent entanglement spreading in (1+1)-dimensional stabilizer circuits with up to 128 qubits. We find that, above an information threshold, agents learn stochastic near-optimal strategies that prevent the system from reaching volume-law entangled states and instead stabilize area-law scaling. These strategies rely on bottlenecks that divide the system and cap the entanglement in the steady state. Crucially, learned strategies are inherently out of equilibrium, require real-time active feedback, and could not be reproduced by simple human-designed control rules. This work establishes the foundations for information-driven individual control of many interacting quantum degrees of freedom, demonstrating the capabilities of reinforcement learning to stabilize and uncover novel critical properties of many-body nonequilibrium steady states.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Cemin, Markus Schmitt, Marin Bukov

item.title: Adversarial Thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2510.08298v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In thermodynamics, an agent's ability to extract work is fundamentally constrained by their environment. Traditional frameworks struggle to capture how strategic decision-making under uncertainty, particularly an agent's tolerance for risk, determines the trade-off between extractable work and probability of success in finite-scale experiments. Here, we develop a framework for nonequilibrium thermodynamics based on adversarial resource theories, in which work extraction is modeled as an adversarial game for an agent extracting work. Within this perspective, we consider a Szilard-type engine as a game isomorphic to Kelly gambling, an information-theoretic model of optimal betting under uncertainty -- but with a thermodynamic utility function. Extending the framework to finite-size regimes, we apply a risk-reward trade-off to find an interpretation of the Renyi divergences in terms of extractable work for a given failure probability. By incorporating risk sensitivity via utility functions, we show that the guaranteed amount of work a rational agent would accept instead of undertaking a risky protocol is given by a Renyi divergence. This provides a unified picture of thermodynamics and gambling, and highlights how generalized free energies emerge from an adversarial setup.
item.dc:creator: Maite Arcos, Philippe Faist, Takahiro Sagawa, Jonathan Oppenheim

item.title: Demon's variational principle for informational active matter
item.description: arXiv:2510.13145v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The interplay between information, dissipation, and control is reshaping our understanding of thermodynamics in feedback-regulated systems. We develop the informational Onsager-Machlup principle, a generalized variational framework that unifies energetic, dissipative, and informational contributions within a single formalism. This framework introduces a conditioned Onsager-Machlup integral to quantify path entropy under specified memory states and enables the derivation of cumulant generating functions for arbitrary observables in systems with measurement and feedback. Our formulation is consistent with stochastic thermodynamics and information thermodynamics. To demonstrate the utility of the IOMP, we apply it to an information swimmer and show that it systematically reproduces the analytical expressions for the mean velocity and higher-order cumulants obtained by a direct approach, while also enabling the calculation of entropy production in the single-measurement case. For repeated measurements and the steady state, we derive approximate analytical expressions by using a Gaussian closure for the distribution of measured velocities. Our analytical results show good agreement with numerical results, except for cases of extreme drag asymmetry.
item.dc:creator: Kento Yasuda, Kenta Ishimoto, Shigeyuki Komura

item.title: Collaboration drives phase transitions towards cooperation in prisoner's dilemma
item.description: arXiv:2602.11601v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The emergence of cooperation among self-interested individuals is a central puzzle across biology and the social sciences. While evolutionary game theory has identified mechanisms such as spatial structure and group selection to sustain cooperation in the prisoner's dilemma, most models assume individuals revise their strategies independently. In reality, social organisms frequently form temporary coalitions to coordinate their decisions. We introduce a \emph{collaboration ring model} to investigate how such joint strategy updating affects the prisoner's dilemma. Individuals update strategies either alone---choosing a best response---or by forming coalitions where actions change only if every member is at least as well off and at least one is strictly better off. Despite individual incentives favouring defection, we show that cooperation emerges through non-equilibrium phase transitions governed by the propensity to collaborate and the benefit of cooperation. Below a critical threshold, defection dominates; above it, cooperation persists through a continuous or a discontinuous transition. Using pair approximation, we derive phase boundaries that align closely with stochastic simulations. Finally, we demonstrate that these results are robust to variations in neighbourhood and coalition size, suggesting that collaborative decision-making is a general mechanism for sustaining cooperation. Our work has potential connections to both the mutualism phenomenon in non-humans and the shared intentionality phenomenon in humans.
item.dc:creator: Joy Das Bairagya, Jonathan Newton, Sagar Chakraborty

item.title: Boundary-Sculpted Arctic Surface in the Cubic Ice Model
item.description: arXiv:2602.24051v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In square ice, domain-wall boundaries freeze the corners behind an arctic curve; strings of reversed arrows, unable to pass each other, give it Tracy-Widom fluctuations. In 3D, they pass around one another. Monte Carlo simulations calibrated on exact 2D results show that boundaries still sculpt an arctic surface in cubic ice, enclosing, by a lower bound, 3% of the box at the largest size. If local equilibrium holds up to it, it lies where the local field reaches the bulk Kasteleyn threshold. Its fluctuations are not Tracy-Widom along lines, and much closer than in 2D to independent strings.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Canals

item.title: Weak ergodicity breaking captured from short-time dynamcis and graph theory
item.description: arXiv:2605.00094v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the onset of weak ergodicity violations in closed quantum many-body systems and focus on cases in which they occur through a transition that is controlled by a model parameter, a scenario called a weak ergodicity-breaking transition. This situation is realized in the Rosenzweig-Porter model and the quantum sun model, which we investigate here. Our analysis is based on representing quantum systems in Fock space and examining the short-time dynamics of density autocorrelation functions. From these, we extract proxies for decay rates for each individual basis state. As a first main result, we show that the distribution of such decay rates captures known weak ergodicity-breaking transitions in both models. As a second main result, we establish a connection between the decay rates of density autocorrelations and graph-theoretical measures. Concretely, we demonstrate that moments of the distribution of the recently introduced graph-energy centrality also detect the weak ergodicity transitions, which is inherited from the behavior of the decay rates. While most numerical tools are limited to small system sizes, the quantities studied in our work can be calculated analytically for large systems of many hundreds of sites and in some cases, even in the thermodynamic limit.
item.dc:creator: Heiko Georg Menzler, Rafa{\l} \'Swi\k{e}tek, Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner

item.title: A reason why we do not observe Schr\"odinger's cats
item.description: arXiv:2605.16148v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A reason is discussed (may be not the only one) for why we do not see any superposition of macroscopic states in the real world. Under the general assumption that quantum macrostates are statistical ensembles of microstates, it is shown that any superposition of macrostates is reduced in a very short time by the unitary dynamics of the ordinary Schr\"odinger equation, deducing the Born rule without having to postulate it. In more detail, the macroscopic and microscopic degrees of freedom are decoupled in the Schr\"odinger equation, yielding an effective stochastic equation for the macroscopic variables, with the ensemble average of the microscopic amplitudes that acts as a self-generated internal white noise. The stochastic equation is shown to be a reducing It\^o equation if some general causality conditions are met, predicting a very quick collapse of any macroscopic superposition upon formation, with probabilities which satisfy the Born rule. In the context of the von Neumann measurement scheme, the relevance of the result is discussed as a simple dynamical solution of the measurement problem.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Siringo

item.title: Ulam Approximation for Nonautonomous Systems: Equivariant Measures and Linear Response
item.description: arXiv:2606.02889v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Despite the prevalence of nonautonomous systems in applications, their statistical properties are much less understood than in the autonomous setting. Building on recent results on response theory for nonautonomous systems, we study the approximation of equivariant families and of their linear response by Ulam-type finite-dimensional reductions. First, we show that coarse-graining procedures associated with the classical Ulam method, and more generally with suitable finite-element projections, such as those often associated with the Koopman/Kolmogorov operator-informed analysis of dynamical systems, provide rigorous approximation of equivariant families for sequential systems with memory loss. Second, for systems whose transfer operators are regularising, we prove that the linear response of the reduced finite-state Markov model converges to the projected linear response of the original system. We illustrate the results with numerical experiments on simple but representative time-dependent diffusive models. These results provide a rigorous foundation for the use of Markov approximations in the study of statistical properties of nonautonomous complex systems which almost invariably relies on finite-scale and finite-precision descriptions of their states and dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Galatolo, Valerio Lucarini, Isaia Nisoli

item.title: Retarded Correlators of Charge Transport in a Magnetic Field
item.description: arXiv:2606.08139v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study charge transport in a magnetized relativistic plasma using kinetic theory within the relaxation-time approximation. By exactly solving the linearized Boltzmann equation in a uniform magnetic field, we obtain an analytic solution for the distribution function in terms of Bessel functions. Using this solution, we compute the full set of retarded current-current correlators and verify the Ward identities. In the hydrodynamic limit, we extract the charge diffusion modes, demonstrating that the transverse diffusion coefficient is strongly suppressed by the magnetic field, scaling as $1/B_0^2$ in the strong-field regime, while the longitudinal diffusion remains unaffected. Furthermore, we analyze the non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in the complex frequency plane, determining their kinematic thresholds and identifying the underlying wave-particle interactions as longitudinal Landau damping and transverse cyclotron damping.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Zhao, Qiuze Sun, Yi Wang, Jin Hu

item.title: Scaling limit of the Random Language Model
item.description: arXiv:2606.28105v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a quantitative theory of the Random Language Model (RLM), an ensemble of stochastic context-free grammars, in a scaling limit where the number of hidden symbols $N \to \infty$ while the grammar temperature $\tilde\epsilon_d \to 0$ at fixed $x = \tilde\epsilon_d \log N$. In this limit, the model admits a controlled description based on a large-deviation principle over rule-usage patterns. A semi-annealed approximation maps the problem to a class of Random Energy Models with nontrivial combinatorics. We show that the RLM exhibits a freezing transition at a critical value $x_c=1/8$, below which rule usage condenses on a subset of preferred rules and language statistics acquire a nontrivial dependence on corpus length. A second characteristic scale at $x=1/2$, associated with the breakdown of Gaussian fluctuations, separates transition and babbling regimes. Across regimes, we derive explicit scaling laws for the number of distinct rules, entropy, and energy, identifying distinct frozen and critical regimes controlled by the interplay of grammar size, corpus length, and temperature. The theory resolves previous ambiguities regarding the existence of a thermodynamic transition and explains the slow approach to the large-$N$ limit as a consequence of the dependence on $\log N$. It further provides a unified framework in which universal statistical properties of language emerge from typical realizations of generative grammars, with implications for both natural language statistics and the behavior of large language models. Heaps' law and Zipf's law are both derived, and the dependence of predictive entropy on context length is rationalized. Comparison with empirical measurements of Heaps' and Zipf's laws yields parameter estimates for real languages.
item.dc:creator: Eric De Giuli

item.title: Statistical mechanics of a three-body Hopfield model with finite connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2607.17234v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A three-body Hopfield model defined on sparse random graphs with finite mean connectivity is studied using a replica-symmetric (RS) analysis. By extending the functional replica framework for conventional two-body finite-connectivity Hopfield models, self-consistent equations for the local-field distribution are derived and solved numerically by population dynamics. At low memory load, the RS analysis shows a discontinuous transition between paramagnetic and retrieval states, accompanied by coexistence of distinct fixed points and an upper spinodal of the retrieval solution. Starting the RS population dynamics from an uninformative finite-amplitude field distribution also leads to a spin-glass-like (SG-like) fixed point at low temperatures, even though the paramagnetic fixed point remains locally stable. As the number of embedded patterns increases, the retrieval solution disappears, while the SG-like RS solutions are found at high load. However, the local instability and thermodynamic inconsistencies of the low-temperature RS solutions indicate the limitations of the RS description of the glassy regime. Finite-size Monte Carlo simulations using population annealing agree well with the RS description of the retrieval branch during heating but exhibit glassy trapping behavior under cooling. Such trapping can occur even for a single embedded pattern, where conventional cross-talk noise among stored patterns is absent, indicating the importance of sparse connectivity and three-body interaction. The characteristic number of embedded patterns separating different solution regimes grows approximately linearly with the mean connectivity, corresponding to finite characteristic load ratios. These results clarify how sparse connectivity and many-body interactions influence the stability and accessibility of retrieval states in associative memory.

item.title: Determining Critical Temperature Differences of Low-Temperature-Differential Stirling Engines: Nonlinear Dynamics Approach
item.description: arXiv:2607.26539v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While the low-temperature-differential (LTD) Stirling engines are innovative engines that can operate with low temperature differentials in our daily life, the problem of determining the critical temperature differences below which the engine ceases to rotate remains unexplored. In this study, we solve this problem using a nonlinear dynamics approach. We derive the self-consistent equations that determine the critical temperature differences as homoclinic bifurcation points of a dynamical model of the LTD Stirling engines. The solutions of the self-consistent equations reveal a combination of parameters that determines the critical temperature differences. This enables us to establish the fundamental design principles for improving the performance of the LTD Stirling engines beyond empirical designs.
item.dc:creator: Momoko Amemiya, Yuki Izumida

item.title: Quantum fluctuation relations in first-detection processes
item.description: arXiv:2608.06194v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive three quantum fluctuation relations for systems undergoing repeated projective measurements. These fluctuation relations characterize the work that can be extracted from a quantum device when a first-detection event triggers a mechanical operation leading to positive work production. The correction to the standard quantum Jarzynski equality depends logarithmically on the mean first-detection time for the time-reversed dynamics. Application of Jensen's inequality leads to fundamental limits on both the total work involved in the repeated measurements and final mechanical operation, and the extracted work alone. An analogous inequality is derived for the work performed exclusively during the sequence of repeated projective measurements. The general case of a device connected to an external environment is also considered.
item.dc:creator: A. Imparato

item.title: Dissipative framework for subsystem dynamics of noninteracting quantum chains
item.description: arXiv:2608.21336v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When only local observables of a many-body quantum system are of interest, it is desirable to formulate a reduced description within the Hilbert space of the corresponding subsystem, with the remaining degrees of freedom traced out and acting as an environment. Assuming initially uncorrelated states and Gaussian environments, we develop a framework for reconstructing the local dynamical generator of noninteracting quantum chains, with polynomial computational effort. As an application, we consider two representative models: a bipartitioned Kitaev chain and a Kitaev chain boundary-coupled to a fully connected free-fermion environment. In both models, strong subsystem-environment coupling leads to non-Markovian dynamics characterized by ballistic spreading of the Lindblad dissipator support within the subsystem. On the other hand, weak coupling to a fully connected environment yields predominantly boundary-localized, Markovian dissipation. Our work highlights the implications of subsystem-environment correlations on the generator of local dynamics, beyond the conventional weak-coupling approximations.
item.dc:creator: Michele Coppola, Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls, Zala Lenar\v{c}i\v{c}

item.title: FrOGS: Discrete Neural Sampler for Independent Alloy Configurations Across Chemical Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2609.02948v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Predicting the thermodynamic properties of an alloy requires sampling its configurations across many chemical conditions and recovering free energies on a common absolute scale. Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is the standard tool, but it requires separate simulations at different conditions, and auxiliary free-energy methods such as thermodynamic integration are used to place results on a common absolute scale. Modern discrete neural samplers typically use reverse KL divergence as the objective and can be mode-seeking or biased. We present Free energy Offering Generative Sampler (FrOGS), a hybrid discrete neural sampler that couples an autoregressive model to a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) to be trained jointly under a single shared loss. FrOGS draws i.i.d. configurations, returns an unbiased estimate of the partition function, and gives consistent estimates of thermodynamic observables. We train a single model across a wide range of chemical conditions to produce estimates on a common absolute free-energy scale. FrOGS matches exact finite-size results on the 2D Ising model and reference phase diagrams for AgPd and CuAu, without mode collapse. We additionally compare to SEGAL, a published autoregressive baseline, and find that only FrOGS recovers the stability range of the CuAu$_3$ phase.
item.dc:creator: Kyucheol Min, Elyssa Hofgard, Tess Smidt

item.title: Universal Defect Statistics in Reverse Quenches
item.description: arXiv:2609.14960v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the generalized Kibble-Zurek mechanism (gKZM) to reverse quench protocols using a stochastic description of defect formation finding that the mean defect density after a reverse quench equals twice the forward quench defect-number variance per unit volume. This relation, universally valid within the stochastic framework of the gKZM, makes the forward quench variance accessible through a reverse quench defect density measurement. We verify the equality analytically and numerically in the uniform one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, and numerically in its bond-disordered variant, including a regime where defect scaling departs from a pure power-law in quench time. Our result also suggests an experimental route to probing quantum critical behavior: reverse quenches that begin and end in the paramagnetic phase may allow to reveal critical exponents using global magnetic-field control and magnetization measurements, without resolving individual defects.
item.dc:creator: Eduard J. Braun, Daniel Rubin, Margaux Cartier, Gerhard Z\"urn, Matthias Weidem\"uller

item.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
item.description: arXiv:2610.16733v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.

item.title: Monodromy Defects of 3D Wilson-Fisher Criticality on the Fuzzy Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.31269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Monodromy line defects arise as boundaries of topological symmetry surfaces, providing a natural route to conformal defects with implications in condensed matter, gauge theories and quantum information. However, their interacting dynamics remains difficult to characterize non-perturbatively. Here we realize monodromy boundary conditions in the fuzzy-sphere regularization by threading a symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We apply this construction to the $Z_2$ twist of the 3D Ising conformal field theory (CFT), the $\pi$-twist of the 3D O(2) CFT, and three inequivalent monodromies of O(3) (centre twist, z-axis $\pi$-twist and reflection). For each defect we extract the low-lying defect spectrum together with bulk-to-defect and defect-defect operator product expansion coefficients, which characterize the operators living on the defect line, their mutual interactions, and how they couple to the critical bulk. Among the resolved low-lying defect primaries we find no relevant scalar perturbation preserving all symmetries of the corresponding defect; the relevant deformations identified break at least one preserved symmetry, providing evidence that these monodromy defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations. For the partial twists of O(3), we derive the flow of the symmetry-preserving untwisted zero-mode mass generated by the bulk interaction. Its weak-coupling runaway near four dimensions motivates a careful distinction between the microscopic absence of pinning, the free reference background, and a possible infrared defect fixed point in three dimensions. These results establish a systematic set of non-perturbative conformal data for monodromy defects beyond the Ising twist, turning the symmetry flux into a tunable knob of the fuzzy-sphere regularization for exploring the response of critical matter to distinct defects.
item.dc:creator: Yin Tang, W. Zhu

item.title: Maximum-Entropy Ensemble of Quantum Subsystems with a Fixed Average State
item.description: arXiv:2610.39712v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The reduced density matrices of Haar-random bipartite states form a fixed-trace version of the Wishart ensemble of random matrices, with an asymptotic eigenvalue density given by the Marchenko-Pastur (MP) law. We establish a similar universal form for the maximum-entropy distribution of mixed states subject to a fixed ensemble average, arguing that its eigenvalue density converges asymptotically to that of the correlated Wishart ensemble (CWE). The density is thus obtained by a free multiplicative convolution formula, which we apply to the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) with a thermal average state to derive a high-temperature leading-order correction to the MP law. We then consider measurement by a random POVM on the purification of the mixed reference state. We show that the resulting mixed-state ensemble is asymptotically equivalent to the CWE, and provide confirming numerical evidence. We return to the TFIM example to compute the entanglement of the system with the ancilla after measurement, and give finite-temperature Page curves for the average entanglement entropies.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Shakeshaft, Christopher David White, Harry J. D. Miller

item.title: The massive phase of the two-dimensional Heisenberg model is stable under small anisotropy
item.description: arXiv:2611.01532v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Polyakov predicted that the classical Heisenberg model on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ has exponentially decaying correlations at every temperature, and proofs of this have recently been posted. We show that the massive phase survives small anisotropy. For every inverse temperature $\beta$ there is $\delta(\beta)>0$ such that the $S^2$-valued model with couplings $\sum_iJ^i\sigma_x^i\sigma_y^i$ has exponentially decaying spin two-point functions, uniformly in finite subgraphs with free boundary conditions and in edge strengths up to $\beta$, whenever all $|J^i-1|\le\delta(\beta)$. The same holds for aligned single-ion anisotropy and for nearly isotropic $O(n)$ models with $n\ge3$. Consequently, for the easy-plane model with couplings $\sigma^x\sigma^x+\sigma^y\sigma^y+\lambda\sigma^z\sigma^z$, the onset of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase, proved by Garban and de Montgolfier for every $\lambda\in(-1,1)$, moves to zero temperature as $\lambda\uparrow1$. These results rest on the annulus crossing bound of Ding, Huang and Yang, used on one finite annulus where the anisotropy is a bounded perturbation, and on a sign-cluster argument with Ginibre's inequality for anisotropic planar energies. Explicit constants of another isotropic proof give decay for $\beta\le c |\log(1-\lambda)|^{1/2}$. For $n\ge4$ and $|J^i-1|\le\delta$ with $\delta$ small, at $\beta\le(1-\varepsilon)|\log\delta|/(2\pi)$ spin one-point functions decay exponentially away from the boundary under every boundary condition, and two-point functions decay, both on the scale $e^{\pi\beta+O(\sqrt{\beta\log\beta})}$. This is the $O(4)$ threshold: for $n=4$ it matches the renormalization-group crossover to leading order; for $n\ge5$ it lies below the prediction. This part is conditional on estimates of a recent manuscript on the $O(4)$ model, which the proof transfers to anisotropic couplings at one scale; only odd observables transfer.
item.dc:creator: Yan Ru Pei

item.title: Exact Transport-Information Correspondence for Distribution-Adaptive Discretization
item.description: arXiv:2611.06059v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Discretization of continuous probability distributions is an operation on the sample space, and the structure induced by this operation cannot generally be determined solely from information geometry. In our recent work on unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), we established a non-arbitrary connection between the transport cost associated with discretization and the information-geometric indistinguishability of continuous probability distributions. Through this transport-information correspondence, UCN quantifies the information-theoretic cost associated with discretization in terms of the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence between nearby continuous distributions characterized by the discretization geometry. In the original UCN construction, discretization is implemented by transporting the probability mass within each cell to its geometric centroid. The resulting transport-information correspondence, however, is derived under specific conditions involving the cell geometry, spatial coverage, and the vanishing-cell-scale limit. In this work, we generalize the local-map discretization framework by allowing an arbitrary representative point for each cell and establish an exact decomposition of the associated transport cost into contributions from the conditional covariance of the probability distribution and the displacement of the representative point from its probability-weighted centroid. Consequently, the resulting transport cost is exactly represented by the expectation of the associated Fisher-induced quadratic form, without requiring uniform cell geometry, complete coverage of the sample space, or an infinitesimal cell-scale limit. The proposed construction thus establishes an exact transport-information correspondence for finite-scale discretization using arbitrary collections of non-overlapping bounded sets.
item.dc:creator: Koretaka Yuge

item.title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
item.description: arXiv:2611.06473v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions. We compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of Ising CFT at nonzero temperature. We conjecture that the QNM TBA framework should also be applicable for describing out-of-equilibrium approach to Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).
item.dc:creator: Zoltan Bajnok, Romuald A. Janik

item.title: Accessing Continuous Monodromy Defects of the 3D Conformal Field Theory on the Fuzzy Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.08102v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Monodromy defects are line defects at the boundary of a topological symmetry surface, around which charged operators acquire a symmetry phase. They probe how a critical system responds to an inserted symmetry flux, but their universal information at strongly coupled fixed points, in particular for a continuous family of twists, remains hard to access. Here we investigate the continuous family of $U(1)$ monodromy defect with fractional twist angles embedded in the three-dimensional $O(2)$ Wilson--Fisher conformal field theory. We realize this continuous family of defects within the fuzzy-sphere framework by threading a fractional Aharonov--Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We observe charged defect operators carrying fractional transverse spins, as a characteristic signature of the imposed monodromy, and a displacement operator close to its protected dimension, supporting the conformal nature of the defect line. Crucially, we resolve no relevant symmetry-preserving scalar, and identify the charge-one defect operators as the only relevant, symmetry-breaking deformations. Assuming the particle--vortex duality, the U(1) monodromy defect maps to a Wilson line of fractional charge in the critical noncompact Abelian Higgs model, and our results then provide evidence that these Wilson lines with fractional charge are locally stable conformal lines.
item.dc:creator: Yin Tang, W. Zhu
